params.purpose: Tool for an artist planning a painting; no original program to match, built from the request alone.
params.question: Build a desktop painting colour assistant: open an image, crop it, view a greyscale value study with N levels, a colour-reduced version with N levels, overlay a composition grid (rule of thirds, Fibonacci spiral, square grid), and for each reduced colour compute a Kubelka-Munk mixing recipe from a user-defined pigment palette (watercolor / acrylic / oil, with transparency per paint).

choices: Yes, but keep it simple at first
params.context: Photo editors like GIMP or Krita can already do greyscale, posterize, crop and grids, and the Mixbox paint-mixing app does Kubelka-Munk mixing. None of them combine it all with your own named pigment palettes (PY/PB/PR codes, transparency) and give mixing recipes for every colour in your image. That combination is what this app adds.
params.question: Similar tools already exist. Should I go ahead and build your all-in-one painting assistant?
